title: Keeping Singapore's Workforce Competitive In Light of Remote Workers From the Region Willing to Work For Less Pay
what_it_is: Keeping Singapore's Workforce Competitive In Light of Remote Workers From the Region Willing to Work For Less Pay

sections.label: Remote working and lower cost countries
sections.summary: Remote working may prompt companies to redistribute activities to lower cost countries to use available manpower.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, remote working may indeed prompt companies to redistribute their activities to take advantage of manpower availability in lower cost countries.

sections.label: Competing on productivity and connectivity
sections.summary: With limited land and manpower, Singapore competes on productivity, connectivity and support for business innovation, not cost alone.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: With limited land and manpower, we no longer compete on cost alone but on productivity, connectivity and ability to support business innovation.

sections.label: Business environment, skills, labour laws
sections.summary: Singapore must strengthen its business environment, sustain skills efforts like SkillsFuture, and review labour laws with tripartite partners while monitoring remote working shifts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: First, we must strengthen our business environment and ensure that Singapore remains the preferred location for trade and investment, particularly in emerging growth areas, such as additive manufacturing and fintech.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Second, we must sustain efforts to help Singaporeans build skills relevant to the global talent marketplace.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: This is why we started the SkillsFuture movement and complemented it with a range of career conversion programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: As for whether labour laws need to be updated, this is an on-going process that takes into account feedback from our tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: We are also actively monitoring shifts in workplace practices due to remote working and sharing views with our international counterparts, to assess the need for policy intervention.

sections.label: Helping workers stay relevant and skilled
sections.summary: Workers need help to stay relevant and skilled so jobs are not substituted or moved overseas, with the Labour Movement working with the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But what it also means is that we need to help our workers stay relevant, skilled, to remain competitive so that these jobs are not substituted or moved overseas so easily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Therefore, I think that the whole eco-system needs to be worked on and this is where the Labour Movement plays an important role, working with the Government, especially on our SGUnited Jobs and Skills programmes.
